method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. A script decoded each registrar, callback thunk, vftable cell and builder call from those bytes and asserted the addresses recorded in the rows. Callers, stores and loads were enumerated from a linear decode of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and script counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Order counts follow the rule of manifests/player_misc_native_call_contract.json. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency, and the item to list compare trees are not copied.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the _isAlive method surfaces and of thirteen native registrations: PlayerBase _getWarpRecastTime, _getNormalBehestTime, _getCompanyBehestTime, _getHamletDefenseScore, _getHamletDefenseScoreAll, _isEnabledGoobbue, _getChocoboGrade, _canStoreItem and _countStoredItem, and AreaBase _countHamletSupplyRanking, _getHamletSupplyRanking, _canRideChocobo and _isWarpRideChocobo. Each row gives the registration site, receiver check, declared argument and return lists, the Lua pushes of every branch including a PlayerBase that is not a MyPlayer, the client field that the callback reads with its writers where traced, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish timer, Chocobo, Goobbue, stored item, hamlet or area content or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/player_misc_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route and the world object chain. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The same count gives 52, 48 and 88 for the registered callers of _getGrandCompanyRank, _getOccupancyContentsTime and _getStoredItem and 6 for _isInn, which agrees with manifests/player_misc_native_call_contract.json and manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor and returns false without calling the callback when the cast gives null. Only _getHamletDefenseScoreAll uses the non-const PlayerBase holder.

argumentReaders.0x005819A0: int, cell tag 0. The callbacks of this record test the cell vector size before each read and call 0x009D22B4 when it is too small.

listBuilders.0x00740250: five ints, registry entry 0, through 0x00727340 for the indexes 3 and 4

returnPushers.note: Each pusher appends its cell to the vector at ExecuteParameters +0x1C. A callback that calls no pusher returns no value to Lua.

The return list builder 0x00728C20 makes one int and the argument list builder 0x0072B440 makes no entry.

The callback 0x0071E4B0 loads the receiver vftable and jumps through the dword at offset +0x16C. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5F70 holds 0x00776340, a bare ret 4 that pushes nothing. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD79C8 holds 0x00705550.

The MyPlayer routine 0x00705550 resolves R through 0x00CC7510, follows [R] and the dword at +0x04 of it to Y, loads S from Y +0x10C and calls the getter 0x0075D260, which returns the dword at S +0x18. It pushes the result as an int through 0x00584F70 into the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.

The routine 0x00578C90 handles the first argument 0x12 through the jump table at 0x00578FDC. The case at 0x00578D32 calls the setter 0x0075D250, which stores its argument at S +0x18. The stored value is 0 when the second argument is -1 and the sum of the second and third arguments otherwise. The only rel32 caller of 0x00578C90 is 0x004DD37D.
xivl-opcodes:opcodes.json lists the clientbound 0x0193 record with the decompAnchor FUN_00578C90 and names this native as the scalar reader of the sub opcode 0x12.

The same record states that the packet header clock is a whole second Unix clock and that the application values are offsets in that unit, so the stored value is an end time in seconds. The unit and the role come from the cited notes and the native name, not from the reader.
The eligibility rule, the reset policy, the server scheduling and the allocation of S before the first 0x0193 record were not established.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x0074A220 pushes the name literal 0x00FD7AF0 at 0x0074A309 and installs the callback 0x006F97C0 through the wrapper 0x0072CD40, which constructs the const AreaBase holder. The return list builder 0x00728C20 makes one int and the argument list builder 0x0072B440 makes no entry.

The callback 0x006F97C0 is a direct member function of AreaBase. It loads the pointer at this +0x60, loads the dword at pointer +0x08 when the pointer is not null and pushes the value, or 0, as an int through 0x00584F70.

The ranking object is 0x0C bytes, allocated by 0x006F3310 and constructed by 0x006F3030 when the pointer at AreaBase +0x60 is null. The refill routine 0x006EDFF0 erases the previous nodes through 0x0071CB60, links the head node at object +0x04 to itself, stores 0 at +0x08, then converts up to 20 wire records through 0x006DCB50 and inserts each through 0x007214B0, which reaches the node insert 0x0071EFC0. That insert adds to the dword at tree +0x08 at 0x0071F053. The AreaBase constructor zeroes the pointer at 0x006F324A.

The inserted elements are unique. 0x007214B0 descends from the root and refuses an element that is equivalent to an existing one under the three key order recorded in _getHamletSupplyRanking, storing 0 in the result flag at 0x007215F1. The count is therefore the number of distinct elements, which can be fewer than the number of nonzero wire records.

The node layout with a head node, a size at +0x08, links at node +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08, a color byte at node +0xC0 and a head flag byte at node +0xC1 is that of an ordered associative container of the era. The class was not named from RTTI.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x0074A370 pushes the name literal 0x00FD7B0C at 0x0074A459 and installs the callback 0x006F97F0 through the wrapper 0x0072CD40, which constructs the const AreaBase holder. The return list builder 0x007437F0 makes int, Utf8String, int, Utf8String, int, int, int, int, int and the argument list builder 0x00728C20 makes one int.

The return list builder 0x007437F0 makes nine entries. The entries 0 and 2 are the registry entry 0 (int), the entry 1 is the registry entry 3 (Utf8String), the entry 3 comes from 0x00740D50 with the registry entry 3 (Utf8String) and the entries 4 to 8 come from the chain 0x0073E4E0, 0x0072CFA0, 0x0072CF40 and 0x0072CEA0, each with the registry entry 0 (int).

The callback 0x006F97F0 reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0, passes the value minus 1 to 0x006E58F0 with six output pointers and pushes the outputs in the order recorded in returns. The byte that 0x006E58F0 returns (node +0xBF) selects between the Utf8String and four ints and the five nils for the positions 3 to 7. The position 8 is pushed after both branches.

The getter 0x006E58F0 starts at the first node of the tree (the node that the head node links at +0x00), steps forward through 0x00717F80 for a positive count and backward through 0x006CE680 for a negative count and tests the final node against the head node. 0x00717F80 and 0x006CE680 call 0x009D22B4 when the iterator holds no tree or the step starts on the head node (the byte +0xC1 is nonzero). The getter copies the dword at node +0xB8, the string at +0x0C, the byte at +0xBE, the string at +0x60, the sign extended word at +0xBC and the dword at +0xB4 to its outputs and returns the byte at +0xBF.

The node fields come from 0x006DCB50 over the 76 byte wire record. The wire dword +0x00 is stored at node +0xB4 and the wire dword +0x04 at node +0xB8. The wire string +0x08 goes to node +0x0C, the wire string +0x28 to node +0x60, the wire word +0x48 to node +0xBC and the wire byte +0x4A to node +0xBE. The byte at node +0xBF is 1 when the first byte of the linkshell string is nonzero.

0x007214B0 inserts a converted element by descent. At each node the element goes left when its points (node +0xB8) are greater than those of the node, or the points are equal and its dword at +0xB4 is smaller, or both are equal and the name compare 0x00446EF0 reports it as less. Otherwise it goes right. The points compare is signed (setg at 0x00721514) and so is the +0xB4 compare (setl at 0x0072150F), so a wire dword of 0x80000000 or more, typed u32le in manifests/hamlet_wire_contract.json, sorts as negative. 0x00446EF0 calls 0x00445B70 over the shorter of the two string lengths and reports less for a negative result. 0x00445B70 compares sign extended chars (movsx) and returns 0 at a NUL that both strings share. The first node that 0x006E58F0 reaches is the leftmost node. Row n is therefore the n-th element by points descending, then the dword +0xB4 ascending, then the name, and not the n-th wire record.

A name that is a proper prefix of another name sorts as less and is not dropped as a duplicate. The Utf8String length at +0x08 appears to count the terminator, because 0x00445BB0 stores the length of the converted text plus 1 at 0x00445BD8, so the shorter-length compare reaches the NUL of the prefix. The length setter was not traced further.

The positions 5, 6 and 7 are the int 0 whenever the byte +0xBF is nonzero. With B the stack pointer after the cookie push at 0x006F981D, the callback zeroes the frame dwords B+0x30 (0x006F98C3), B+0x34 (0x006F98C7) and B+0x24 (0x006F98CB) before the call of 0x006E58F0 and pushes them at 0x006F9947, 0x006F9959 and 0x006F996B. scriptSurfaces.registration: None. No registrar of the 0x00CCCAD0 shape pushes the name. The literal 0x0110F068 has one code reference at 0x00D08658 and the literal 0x0110F204 has one at 0x00D1110E, both inside metatable __index closures.

receivers.note: The __index closure of the instance metatable. A live instance resolves _isAlive through the class chain to the ActorBaseClass function. A released instance resolves it to the global __lge_isAlive.
The __index closure of the IndividualRef metatable. It answers only the key _isAlive, with the C closure 0x00D11010.

returns.note: Lua boolean. 0x00CF3320 calls 0x00DCE360, which stores the Lua type tag 1 and a value that is 1 for a nonzero argument.

scriptSurfaces.behavior: Called as a method with no argument. On a live script instance the ActorBaseClass function returns true. On a released script instance every key lookup is redirected to a global function, so _isAlive returns false and any other method call returns nil. On an IndividualRef the C closure asks the engine whether the referenced control still answers, and pushes the answer as a bool. No yield.

facts.claim: The literal _isAlive at 0x0110F068 has one code reference, the push at 0x00D08658 inside the instance __index closure 0x00D085B0. The closure runs 0x00CE1BB0 on the instance record and, after a true answer, compares the key with the literal through 0x00445D60. A match pushes the string __lge_isAlive (literal 0x0110F074) and any other key pushes the string whose pointer sits at 0x0130D50C (__lge_returnNil). It then reads that global through 0x00CF3A50. After a false answer the closure continues at 0x00D086C3 without the substitution.

The bootstrap source at 0x0110E680, which 0x00CD8E6E passes to the loader, defines the global function __lge_isAlive that returns false and the global function __lge_returnNil that returns nil. The source text was read from the executable bytes.

0x00CE1BB0 is the released test. It returns true at once when the byte at record +0x7E is set. It proceeds only when the dword at record +0x08 equals 0x00010009 (0x0130D500) and not 0x0001000A (0x0130D504), and otherwise returns false. On proceeding it casts the object at record +0x00 from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to LuaTentativeControl (0x012C0828) without a null test and calls virtual slot 3 through 0x00CCCB10. A false answer runs 0x00CD2A50 on record +0x50, sets the byte +0x7E and returns true. A true answer returns false.

The literal _isAlive at 0x0110F204 has one code reference, the load at 0x00D1110E inside the IndividualRef __index closure 0x00D110B0. A nine byte compare against the key pushes the C closure 0x00D11010 at 0x00D11122. That closure reads the userdata, calls 0x00CE19C0 with the two dwords of the reference and pushes the returned byte as a bool through 0x00CF3320. 0x00CE19C0 takes the second dword as the address of a control pointer, casts the control from LuaControl to LuaTentativeControl and calls virtual slot 4 through 0x00CCCB20 with the first dword. The slot answer is returned unchanged.

The base class vftable of LuaTentativeControl (0x0110E360) holds 0x006D6F80 in slot 3 and 0x0094F630 in slot 4. Both set the low byte of eax to 1 and return. The vftables of GroupBase (0x00FD53CC), ItemBase (0x00FD5484) and WidgetHandle (0x00FD57D4) name LuaTentativeControl in their class hierarchy and hold 0x00712B40 in both slots. That routine is a bare ret 8.

An IndividualRef _isAlive over a GroupBase, ItemBase or WidgetHandle control answers true. 0x00CE19C0 pushes two arguments at 0x00CE1A10 and 0x00CE1A15 and reaches slot 4 through the thunk 0x00CCCB20, which loads the slot with mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x10]; jmp eax. The bare ret 8 at 0x00712B40 balances those two pushes and leaves eax holding 0x00712B40, so the low byte al is 0x40. 0x00CE19C0 keeps it in bl across 0x00CC77F0 (0x00CE1A29, 0x00CE1A38) and returns it. 0x00D11010 passes it to 0x00CF3320, which reads one byte and calls 0x00DCE360, whose setne stores 1 for a nonzero value, so Lua receives true.

The slot 3 call of the released test pushes one argument at 0x00CE1C25 through the thunk 0x00CCCB10 (slot at +0x0C). The base routine 0x006D6F80 is ret 4 and balances it. A control whose slot 3 is the bare ret 8 at 0x00712B40 would leave esp 4 bytes off inside 0x00CE1BB0, and the answer would be the low byte 0x40, a nonzero value. That case needs a script instance whose record dword +0x08 is 0x00010009 over a GroupBase, ItemBase or WidgetHandle control. Whether any such instance exists is unknown.
The classes that carry the kind 0x00010009, the engine event that makes slot 3 answer false, and the classes that override slots 3 and 4 with a body were not enumerated.

The byte at record +0x7E marks a released or undefined reference, so the substitution makes _isAlive return false for a script instance whose engine control is gone. The role comes from the tentative control name, the released test shape and the bootstrap functions.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order.

Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time. The argument and result use of the scripts was not decoded for this record.
Caller, store and load searches are linear decodes of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. An absent store is not proof that no store exists.

The object S, the score object at MyPlayer +0x154 and the ranking object at AreaBase +0x60 are read without a null test by their callbacks except where a row says otherwise. The run-time effect of a null object was not run.
The item sets behind 0x00714440 and 0x007153D0 are compare trees over item numbers. They are not copied or enumerated here.
The ranking container is described from its node layout and its comparison and insert routines. It was not named from RTTI.
The release of a script instance and a script instance of the kind 0x00010009 over a GroupBase, ItemBase or WidgetHandle control were not traced or run.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish timer, Chocobo, Goobbue, stored item, hamlet score, hamlet ranking or area content, or server behavior.

The selection of the natives is by the request of this record and the static script names in xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. It is not an execution trace and not a census of the natives that a script reaches on a given path.
